source_refs.note: c) Identification of Calcium (Ca²⁺) radical: a main subheading of 16.7 Tests for identification of basic radicals, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 345-346.

blocks.text: Take 4 g solid sample in a clean test tube. Dissolve it in 10 cm³ distilled water. Make two parts of this solution for further tests.

blocks.caption: Identification of calcium radical
rows: To one part, add NaOH solution.
White precipitate is formed which does not dissolve in excess of NaOH solution.
To the second part of the above solution, add aqueous ammonia.
Only a slight turbidity appears or No precipitate is formed.
